_doc: CHARATAN dating cabinet = DATA only (cabinet #7, built 2026-07-16 following control/CABINET_METHOD.md). Charatan dates by the FERRARA ERA SYSTEM: bit style (tapered vs Double Comfort), DC/X shape-code suffixes, the circled-L '£' Lane stamp, CP stem-logo generations, and the shank-engraving evolution. SOURCES (local-first): pipedia mirror staging/pipedia/Dating_of_Charatans.json (Fabio Ferrara study of 2000+ pipes from the Basciano/Lubinski stock -- THE master reference) + Charatan.json (main article; its 'Memories of Charatan Pipes' (Ivy Ryan) is flagged BY PIPEDIA as containing misinformation -- do NOT source from it). DISAGREEMENTS encoded wide + noted: Reuben's death 1960 (Ferrara) vs 1962 (Ken Barnes interview); Dunhill acquisition April 1976 (Ferrara, documented) vs 1978 (main article); Lane era start 'often quoted' 1950 vs sole-distributorship 1955.

history_anchors._doc: 1951 CATALOGUE ANCHORS (primary, self-dated Festival-of-Britain issue): 'Established as manufacturers in 1863'; addresses = Charatan Pipes Ltd, 18 Jermyn St Haymarket S.W.1 + 49 Whitcomb St Leicester Sq W.C.2, FACTORY: Minories E.C.3; shape numbers all PLAIN (incl. 0-prefixed 014/099/0104...), ZERO DC/X suffixes -> corroborates the Ferrara post-1960 suffix cliff; mouthpieces = tapered standard + optional Dental / Solid Bite (no Double Comfort in 1951); 1951 shape names: Newmarket, Dresden China, Lonsdale, Lovat, Artist, Bell Dublin, Lumberman, Huntsman, Ritz, Zulu, Small Golfer, Prince, Cutty, Giants 42/43/44; free ANY-SHAPE bespoke service + free exchange/alteration invitation enclosed with each pipe. FERRARA ERAS: (1) Frederick 1863-1910 Mansell St then Prescot St (meerschaum first; first all-handmade English briars -- 'Charatan's Make'). (2) Reuben 1910-1960/62 (Grosvenor St later). (3) First Lane era 1961-1965 (widow sold to Lane Ltd; DC stem = the one Lane innovation). (4) Second Lane era 1965-1976 (Ben Wade machines arrive 1965; some freehands commissioned to Preben Holm + Willmer). (5) First Dunhill era 1977-1981 (Dunhill bought Lane mid-1976; Grosvenor St closed March 1982). (6) Second Dunhill era 1982-1987 = Parker/Hardcastle factory, Forest Rd Walthamstow. (7) Russell era 1988-2000 = production in Saint-Claude FRANCE (Butz-Choquin said to make them; the 'dark period'). (8) New Dunhill era 2000+ = Colin Fromm, Invicta, Chatham; per Dunhill MD, made in the Dunhill factory since 2022. Barry Jones (master carver) era ~1955-1977 -> left for Tilshead/James Upshall with Kenneth Barnes 1978. SUB-BRANDS/SECONDS (own rules): Mountbatten (apprentice-made), London Straight Grain, International Selection, Falstaff, Samirva, Vauxhall, Britannia, Benlet; Ben Wade (Lane, post-1965); Chippendale = Belvedere series for Tinder Box (encoded as a line). Pre-Lane records lost in a factory fire -> pre-1950 dating leans on hallmarks + features.

brand_marks.physical: CP stem logo in generations: very FINE with C penetrating P (until 1960) -> thicker, C still penetrates (1961-1977) -> C joined but NOT penetrating (from ~1980) -> distinct Dunhill-era vs Russell-era shapes. Circled £ (Lane trademark) on shank 1955-c.1980. Chippendale pipes carry CD instead of CP. Shape codes: plain numbers pre-1961; DC suffix (Double Comfort) or X suffix (saddle, no DC) from 1961.

table.note: 'France' marking = Russell era (production moved to Saint-Claude 1988-2000)
London-praising markings ran until the 2nd Dunhill era ended (1987); they disappear under Russell. LOW conf: post-2000 Chatham pipes may reference London again -- verify

line_years._notes: supreme s: introduced by Lane 1957 -> FLOOR. underboar: own-catalogue line with metal stinger, 'made from 1920 to 1930 (approx.)' -> a hair of slack each side, approx flagged. chippendale: the Belvedere series sold for Tinder Box in the FIRST Dunhill era, CD stem logo. ★1951 CATALOGUE MINED (2026-07-18, 'FESTIVAL OF BRITAIN ISSUE, 1951' self-dated, OCR in brand_research\charatan_dating\catalogue_ocr\): the FIVE 1951 qualities = SUPREME / SELECTED / SPECIAL / DE LUXE / DE LUXE SANDBLAST -- so Supreme+Selected+Special exist PRE-LANE (by 1951); 'EXECUTIVE' and 'BELVEDERE' are NOT among the 1951 qualities and first show in our 1964/1965 Lane flyers (Straight Grain ladder: Executive->Selected->Supreme->Supreme S.100->S.200->CORONATION) -> an Executive- or Belvedere-graded pipe LEANS Lane-era-or-later, but ABSENCE NEVER DATES -- kept as a lean, not a bracket. Coronation (top grade, $250 in 1965) = candidate 1953-coronation name, unverified. NOT encoded (no intro years documented): the pre-1950 grade starts (records burned; note 'supreme s' must be matched before bare 'supreme' would be), Free Hand / FH (used 1957-1967/68 per the main article -- single source, sizes varied; park as _note_verify), Double Comfort as a LINE name (it is a BIT STYLE -> bit_style channel), Danish-made freehands of the 2nd Lane era (Preben Holm/Willmer -- inconsistent by design). ★1951-CATALOG FLOORS (2026-07-22, image-read, brand_research/charatan_dating/charatan_1951_catalog_facts.md): the maker's own 1951 catalog names the five qualities SUPREME/SELECTED/SPECIAL/DE LUXE/DE LUXE SANDBLAST -> floors 1951 for supreme/selected/special/de luxe (may antedate; floor = first documented evidence; 'supreme s' stays 1957+ as the distinct later stamp). Same catalog, image-verified: shank stamp CHARATAN'S MAKE / LONDON ENGLAND + CP stem monogram + shape number on shank = the 1951 forms; 1951 addresses Jermyn St SW1 / factory Minories EC3 / Whitcomb St WC2; shape-numbering convention: appended digits = size/length variants (12/180/102, 14/140/1400, 99/990/199); Giants 42/43/44 only in Selected/Supreme quality.

feature_era._doc: The Ferrara system, encoded. Bit style + shape-code suffixes are the sharpest cliffs: tapered = NEVER after 1960; DC/X suffix = ONLY after 1960. The £ and CP generations bracket the middle eras.

table.label: tapered mouthpiece = definitely pre-Lane (Ferrara: 'never tapered' after 1960)
Double Comfort bit = after 1960 (the one Lane innovation; Charatan records say 1950s intro but DC-as-standard = 1961+ -- sources noted, wide honest floor 1961)
DC suffix after the shape number = post-1960
X suffix (saddle bit, no DC) = post-1960
circled-L Lane trademark = 1955 (US sole distributorship) to c.end-1980 (Dunhill kept it briefly); ABSENCE never dates -- factory often forgot the stamp / European-market pipes lack it
block-capitals MADE BY HAND = 1958-1965/66 (introduced 1958; the 3-line block variant ran ~6 months in 1965)

match: made by hand in city of london
table.label: script 'Made by Hand -In- City of London' = 1965/66-1979 (evolved with block/script variants -- main article + Ferrara)
'CHARATAN of London' marking first appears in the Russell era (1988+)
very fine CP with C penetrating P = until 1960
C joined but NOT penetrating P = from c.1980
CD stem logo = Chippendale (Belvedere for Tinder Box, first Dunhill era)

shape number stamped ALONGSIDE the nomenclature on the LEFT shank side = pre-1960 (vkpipes Selected-56 listing, verbatim 'before 1960, as the shape number is situated alongside the nomenclature on the left side of the shank'; NOT in Ferrara -- single specialist source, LOW; describe as 'shape number left' / 'shape number alongside nomenclature' in lettering evidence)

stamped_year._doc: Generic channel; Charatan rarely stamps years, but silver-banded early pipes carry hallmarks (Rudy Tieman examples: 1921-22 straight, 1925-26 bent) -> exact years once generic.json UK charts land.
